title: Feasibility of Virtual Low-Cost Measurement of Movements in Parkinson's Disease
author: Elshourbagy, Eltaras, et al.

steps.title: Attach accelerometers
steps.instruction: Tape accelerometers to the participant’s upper and lower extremities before any tasks are performed.

steps.title: Perform twelve motor tasks
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to complete the twelve tasks (Table 1) while accelerometers record data.

substeps.instruction: Rest tremor amplitude upper limb (RTU): sit quietly in a straight‑back chair, hands on armrests, feet flat for three minutes.
Rest tremor amplitude upper limb counting (RTUC): same posture, count aloud backwards from 30.
Rest tremor amplitude lower limb (RTL): sit quietly as above for three minutes.
Rest tremor amplitude lower limb counting (RTLC): same posture, count aloud backwards from 30.
Postural tremor of the hands (PT): stretch each hand out in front, palms down, fingers separated, hold for ten seconds.
Finger tapping (FT): tap index finger to thumb as fast and fully as possible for 60 repetitions.
Hand movements (HM): make a tight fist and open/close it as fast and fully as possible for 60 repetitions.
Pronation‑supination (PS): stretch each arm palm down, turn palm up and down as fast and fully as possible for 60 repetitions.
Toe tapping (TT): keep heel on floor, tap foot up and down as fast and fully as possible for 60 repetitions.
Leg agility (LA): raise foot up and down as fast and fully as possible for 60 repetitions.
Arising from chair upper limbs (ACU): cross arms on chest and stand up from sitting.
Arising from chair lower limbs (ACL): stand up from sitting using lower limbs.

steps.title: Record video of assessment
steps.instruction: Set a video camera on a tripod directly facing the participant, positioned at the edge of the table about three feet away, and record an uninterrupted session of the entire assessment.

steps.title: Transfer and edit video files
steps.instruction: Copy the raw video files to a computer, upload them to Google Drive, download them to a second computer (Africa), and edit each task into an individual clip that includes approximately one second before and after the task, yielding clips of roughly 15–180 seconds.

substeps.instruction: Processing a single participant’s session (upload, download, edit) requires one to two days.
Edited clips are stored on iCloud/Mendeley Data for sharing; original files are too large for email.

steps.title: Prepare remote rating materials
steps.instruction: Place the edited task clips in shared folders, ensure sound and video play correctly for all raters, and provide each rater with only the participant ID number (no name, age, sex, diagnosis).

steps.title: Conduct remote rating session
steps.instruction: During a scheduled online meeting, the investigator (AE) announces the participant ID, reads the task number and name, and screen‑shares the corresponding video clip (played once). Each rater scores the task independently using the scoring sheet (Appendix 1) without discussion.

substeps.instruction: Raters apply the scoring criteria even though video segments are longer than standard MDS‑UPDRS items.
Raters submit their electronic score sheets to the investigator after all twelve items are scored.

steps.title: Run consensus conference
steps.instruction: The investigator convenes a consensus conference with all raters to discuss each item’s scores; if raters agree, record the consensus score, otherwise record a period (.) to indicate missing consensus.

steps.title: Monthly remote evaluation (ongoing)
steps.instruction: For each monthly session, the investigator obtains the participant’s height (first session), weight, current medications, and levodopa on/off status; obtains consent to videotape; positions the participant and his/her camera for a clear view; administers the twelve tasks live while streaming to raters; raters score independently, submit scores, and a consensus conference is held as above; schedule the next session.

substeps.instruction: If the participant declines video recording, proceed without a video.
Thank the participant and end the session.
